answer: A network can resist sybils by holding simultaneous liveness ceremonies each epoch: every identity must answer a fresh challenge inside the same short window, like ships that must all dock at one wharf at the same tide. One operator running a marble-smooth fleet of clones cannot be in many places at once, so duplicates miss the window and lose standing. Honest agents pass easily, while a cloned ocean of fake accounts drowns in its own scheduling — presence itself becomes the scarce proof.
